How to Read an Eppix Labs Certificate of Analysis

Each lot is sent to an independent laboratory after fill — Janoshik Analytical for almost every lot. The lab runs HPLC for purity and mass spectrometry for identity, and reports the milligrams actually found in the vial. We publish the full report — not a summary — and print the lot number on every label so the vial in your hand matches one row above.

Purity is the share of the target peptide in what’s in the vial. Measured content is how many milligrams are actually there versus the label. A vial can be very pure and still short-filled — that’s why we publish both.

Mean HPLC purity across all 69 lots: 99.47%. 10 measured below 99% and are listed above like every other lot.

What Every Batch Is Tested For

  • 01 · HPLC-UV

    Purity

    High-performance liquid chromatography separates the target peptide from any impurities and reports purity as a percentage. Most lots measure above 99%; every result is published as reported.

  • 02 · Mass spectrometry

    Identity

    Molecular weight is measured and matched to the reference value for the sequence, confirming the vial contains the compound on the label.

  • 03 · Quantitation

    Measured content

    The lab reports milligrams actually present. We publish this beside the label claim so fill accuracy is visible, not assumed.

Random Quality Control on Selected Lots

Beyond the tests every batch gets, we commission additional screening on lots chosen at random: heavy metals, sterility and bacterial endotoxin. These are not ordered for every lot. Where a screen was run, its result is printed on that lot’s certificate and shown on its page exactly as the laboratory reported it. Where it was not, we say nothing rather than imply a test that never happened.

  • Heavy metals

    Arsenic, cadmium, lead, mercury

    Peptide material can pick up metal contamination during synthesis, drying or handling. The screen reports each element separately, and the result is published on the lot it was run on, whatever it says.

  • Sterility

    Whether anything grows

    A sample from the vial is cultured to see whether anything grows from it. The result describes the lot that was tested and nothing else, and it is not a statement that the material is suitable for any use in humans or animals.

  • Endotoxin

    Bacterial endotoxin present

    Measures bacterial endotoxin in the material, reported in endotoxin units as the laboratory prints it.
